CFO at Tide Pod maker P&G on US shoppers:

"One end of the consumer spectrum is doing very well. I think they see their wealth increasing. They see the stock market playing to their advantage. We do see lower income consumers struggling paycheck to paycheck. They are not struggling to the point where we see significant trade down into private label or we see them exiting categories or reducing consumption significantly. But yeah, we see a bifurcation of the consumer, at least in our categories."

As semiconductor stocks shed value, comparing two ETFs provides a valuable lesson on leverage.

While the iShares Semiconductor ETF $SOXX is down 25% from its peak, the 3x leveraged $SOXL has plunged nearly two-thirds. 📉 yhoo.it/4vRHNqf

🇰🇷 South Korea’s chip rout triggered another circuit breaker overnight, with the Kospi plunging before buyers cut the loss.

📉 The same leverage lesson is playing out in the US. $SOXX is down roughly 25% from its June peak, while its 3x counterpart $SOXL has lost nearly two-thirds.

🧮 A 25% loss needs a 33% rebound to recover. A 63% loss needs roughly 170%.

🚨 Leverage makes the fall faster. It also makes the climb back much steeper.
Semiconductor stocks are flashing red. But under the market's hood, the rally is still running green. yhoo.it/4vTBrqo

🔴 Chip stocks are falling out of bed. The $SOX briefly broke below 11,000 Tuesday and is down over 25% from its June high.

💾 $SKHY hit a US all-time low, $MU has lost over $450 billion in market value since its June record high, and $SNDK has been cut by more than half.

🟢 But the S&P 500 equal-weight index hit a record high Tuesday, nearly three-quarters of S&P 500 stocks are up in July, and the advance-decline line also set a record.

⚠️ As long as those broader breakouts hold, the chip crash remains a sector problem. A reversal would show the damage is spreading.

$F just delivered a Q2 earnings beat, and upped its 2026 guidance thanks to strong profit growth.

Ford's full-year adjusted EBIT is now $10 billion to $11 billion, up from $8.5 billion to $10.5 billion.

Watches and jewelery outperformed other divisions, with organic growth reaching 9% for the half and 11% in the second quarter, lifting revenue to €5.22bn and profit 9% higher to €831m.
